title: What became of the Owls after Frank left
summary: Bill kept the Owls briefly; Eddie Miller's departure left a hole and Steve Massico took over.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Oh, I never did understand what happened to the Owls after you left. The trumpet player kept it.

And how long did it last? He didn't last very long over there. Because he went back to the business there. That was right after Huey Long came in there and put all of these loan sharks out of business. But Bill kept it up with his brother-in-law. That they'd lend you half a dollar on Monday. They had this black trade down there. They'd lend you half a dollar on Monday. And you gave them back 75 cents on a Friday on payday. And Bill said, well, I spoke to him after that. But I didn't want to have anything personal to do with it. And he says, I had to quit. He says, because I'd lose too much money. He says, down there, if I played at night, he says, you get these blacks. And he says, if you don't get the 75 cents on a Saturday, he said, well, you wouldn't get the money at all. So he said, so he, then, well, Eddie Miller left us. When Eddie Miller left us, that was a big hole in our band, I'll tell you that.

That was about, oh, I guess about six months or seven months before we broke up. And then we put Steve Massico. You remember Steve Massico? Man, Steve played pretty good. He honked it out real good. He had a good beat and everything else. But he was such a trifling. I said, Richard Gooden. Time to get on the bandstand. We didn't play, but about four choruses, three tunes. And then you'd take 20 minutes off. You couldn't find him at the end of 20 minutes. He related to Buttsy? Yeah, Buttsy's brother. And, uh, in fact, he was a hell of a lot better saxophone player than Buttsy was a drummer, I'll tell you that. And, uh, according to me, now that's my own opinion. I don't know, I don't know whether you agree with him.
